title: Kansas State 35, Oklahoma 7: The 2003 Big 12 Title Game Upset
question: Who beat undefeated No. 1 Oklahoma in the 2003 Big 12 Championship Game?
answer: No. 13 Kansas State beat No. 1 Oklahoma 35-7 in the Big 12 Championship Game on December 6, 2003, at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City. OU still finished No. 1 in the BCS standings and played LSU for the national title.
summary: Kansas State stunned unbeaten No. 1 Oklahoma 35-7 in the 2003 Big 12 Championship. Darren Sproles ran for 235 yards, yet OU still reached the BCS title game.
body: Few Sooner seasons felt as unstoppable as 2003 did in November. Oklahoma arrived at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City on December 6, 2003, unbeaten and ranked No. 1. It left with one of the most stunning losses in program history: Kansas State 35, Oklahoma 7.

The 13th-ranked Wildcats leaned on two stars. Quarterback Ell Roberson completed 10 of 17 passes for 227 yards and four touchdowns. Tailback Darren Sproles ran for 235 yards on 22 carries, the most any opponent had gained against Oklahoma to that point, and added a 60-yard touchdown on a screen pass just before halftime. K-State outgained OU 519 yards to 398, and Oklahoma's quarterback was intercepted twice.
For Kansas State, it was a landmark night: its first conference football championship since 1934.

The fallout made the game even more famous. Oklahoma dropped to No. 3 in the polls but remained No. 1 in the final BCS standings, which sent the Sooners to the Sugar Bowl to play LSU for the national championship. LSU won that game 21-14, and the split between the polls and the BCS became a talking point in the debate over how college football picked its champion.
For trivia purposes, remember the number 35-7. It is a reminder that a conference title game can upend a season, even for a team that had looked like one of the best in Sooner history.
